note: ILLUSTRATIVE DEMO FIXTURE. Each preset describes, in words prepared by people, how the demo strategies might be affected by a hypothetical change. These are NOT climate projections or model outputs. Unsupported slider combinations return SCENARIO_NOT_SUPPORTED.

presets.label: 20% more rain
presets.description: What if every month had a fifth more rain?

explanation: With less rain, tanks may store less water after Maha, which matters most for the Yala season.
Short, lower-water crops in Yala are generally less exposed than a second rice crop.

current-rice-rice.feasibilityReason: Yala rice may not have enough stored water in a drier year.

addRisk.text: Under 20% less rain, the Yala rice crop is the most exposed part of this rotation.

current-rice-rice.summary: Yala rice becomes riskier because it relies on stored water.

addRisk.text: Less April–May rain could stress mung bean at establishment.

alt-rice-mung-bean.summary: Slightly more risk, but mung bean still needs much less water than rice.

alt-rice-cowpea-sunn-hemp.feasibilityReason: Cover crop establishment in July–September becomes even less likely.

addRisk.text: The sunn hemp cover may need to be skipped in a drier year.

alt-rice-cowpea-sunn-hemp.summary: Cowpea likely still possible; the cover crop is doubtful.

explanation: More rain could fill tanks better, but heavy rain also brings waterlogging risk for dry-land crops.
Rice is less affected by wet fields than legumes.

current-rice-rice.summary: More stored water could support Yala rice.

alt-rice-mung-bean.feasibilityReason: Wetter Aprils raise waterlogging risk for mung bean.

addRisk.text: Waterlogging and pod rot risk increase with more rain.

alt-rice-mung-bean.summary: Waterlogging becomes a bigger concern for mung bean.

alt-rice-cowpea-sunn-hemp.feasibilityReason: More rain may help the cover crop establish.

addRisk.text: Cowpea may suffer in waterlogged patches.

alt-rice-cowpea-sunn-hemp.summary: Cover crop may establish better, but cowpea faces waterlogging risk.

explanation: Warmer temperatures increase how fast soil and crops lose water, even if rainfall stays the same.
Very high temperatures at flowering can reduce grain and pod setting in many crops.

addRisk.text: Heat during flowering in the hot Yala months may reduce rice grain filling.

current-rice-rice.summary: More water loss and heat stress during Yala.

addRisk.text: Heat at flowering can reduce pod setting.

alt-rice-mung-bean.summary: Some heat stress; still lower water needs than rice.

alt-rice-cowpea-sunn-hemp.summary: Cowpea and sunn hemp are generally heat tolerant; little change in this illustrative view.

explanation: Hotter and drier conditions together are the toughest case for the Yala season.
Strategies that avoid a second rice crop are generally less exposed in this illustrative view.

current-rice-rice.feasibilityReason: In this illustrative case, Yala rice would likely lack water.

addRisk.text: High chance of Yala rice failure under hotter, drier conditions.

current-rice-rice.summary: Yala rice is unlikely to be possible.

alt-rice-mung-bean.feasibilityReason: Mung bean may still be possible if planted right after harvest to use early rains.

addRisk.text: Heat and dry spells could reduce mung bean yields.

alt-rice-mung-bean.summary: Possible but riskier; timing becomes critical.

alt-rice-cowpea-sunn-hemp.feasibilityReason: Cowpea is hardy, but the cover crop is unlikely without water.

addRisk.text: The cover crop would probably need to be dropped.

alt-rice-cowpea-sunn-hemp.summary: Cowpea may cope best; the cover crop likely fails.
